marks.gloss_en: the mishna (39a): the outer gums that were damaged or scraped, and the inner ones that were uprooted [are blemishes]
before eating it certainly helps it, like a medicine
loose -- it certainly helps it
in the field -- it certainly helps it
תא שמע: ואת שתי הכליות -- not one kidney, not three; ותניא אידך: יסירנה -- to include one kidney. If no creature is born with one, the baraitot dispute whether an internal lack is a lack
'and the two kidneys' (Lev 3:4) -- and not one with one kidney
דכולי עלמא יש בריה באחת וחסרון מבפנים שמיה חסרון, ולא קשיא: כאן כשנבראה בשתים וחסרו, כאן כשנבראה באחת מעיקרא
Rav Chiyya bar Yosef: all agree there is a creature [born] with one [kidney]
אלא, הכא ביש בריה מעיקרא קמיפלגי (= p_kelayot_hinge_beriya)
rather, here they dispute whether there is a creature [with one kidney] from the outset: one master holds there is, the other that there is not
דכולי עלמא אין בריה באחת וחסרון מבפנים שמיה חסרון, ולא קשיא: כאן שחסרה קודם שחיטה, כאן שחסרה לאחר שחיטה
R' Yochanan: here [the disqualifying baraita] -- where it became lacking before slaughter
מאי קאמר? ותו, רבי יהושע בן קפוצאי היינו תנא קמא! -- the baraita asks what the te'omet is and answers about the inner region; and RYbK says what the first tanna says

חסורי מיחסרא והכי קתני -- the baraita is defective; it teaches the inner gums' extent, that damaged or scratched ones are not slaughtered but uprooted ones are, and RYbK and RChbA each go further (= the reconstructed props at 39a.13-14)
what are the inner [gums]? from the te'omet inward, and the te'omet itself is as inward

והא דומיא דשלש קתני, מה שלש מעיקרא, אף אחת מעיקרא -- the baraita lists one kidney alongside three, and three are from the outset, so one is from the outset too. Unanswered: the stam turns to אלא (39a.22)

the baraita as cited: what is the te'omet? from the te'omet inward, and the te'omet itself is as inward. RYbK: one slaughters only for the outer ones. RChbA: one pays no attention to the te'omet at all
RYbK: one slaughters only for the outer ones; for inner ones that were uprooted we do not slaughter
an internal lack of a limb counts as a lack
if for consecrated animals: 'blind or broken' (Lev 22:22) is written
horn 1: 'it shall be complete to be accepted' (Lev 22:21) -- complete, yes; lacking, no
there is no creature [born] with one [kidney]; this one became lacking
its nose that was pierced, or damaged, or split [is a blemish]
limb 1: it ate and was not healed -- it is a blemish retroactively
the practical difference is misuse of its redemption money: if retroactive, one misuses it; if from now on, one does not
Shmuel read of him: 'the lame take the prey' (Isaiah 33:23)
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: provided they are [spaced in] thirds
the nostrils pierced one into the other -- from the outside, this is a blemish
